atoms.name: Pipeline timing basics
atoms.one_line: Time = (k + n - 1) x cycle; ideal speedup tends to k for long programs.

atoms.name: Cycle time and stage balance
atoms.one_line: Cycle = slowest stage + register delay; splitting the longest stage helps until the next stage limits.

atoms.name: CPI with stalls and speedup
atoms.one_line: CPI = 1 + sum of (fraction x stall cycles); speedup = time per instruction ratio = CPI / frequency.

atoms.name: Data dependences
atoms.one_line: RAW is a true dependence; WAR and WAW are name dependences; track writer, reader and register.

atoms.name: Forwarding
atoms.one_line: A result goes from a pipeline register to a later stage input; load-use still stalls one cycle in a five-stage pipeline.

atoms.name: Control hazards
atoms.one_line: Branch penalty = resolve stage minus one; prediction removes the penalty for correct guesses; delay slot runs the next instruction.

atoms.name: Structural hazards
atoms.one_line: Shared port or multi-cycle EX stage stalls followers; stalls = ceiling of delay minus one.

atoms.name: Pipeline timing diagrams
atoms.one_line: Draw per-stage start and finish times; each stage waits for the previous stage and the previous instruction.
